source: Web research 2026-10-04: platform official blogs and earnings transcripts, Google Search Central, Reuters Institute DNR 2026, IAMAI-Kantar, CMI, Upwork, Redseer; numbers copied from the source's own words where the page was read (fallback routes: browser-UA fetch, Google News RSS).

items.name: AI Overviews and zero-click search eat organic clicks
items.one_line: When Google shows an AI summary, far fewer searchers click any result, so ranking #1 no longer guarantees traffic.

evidence.claim: Ahrefs update (Dec 2025 GSC data, 300,000 keywords): AI Overviews correlate with a 58% lower CTR for the top-ranking page, up from 34.5% in April 2025; 'The forecasted rate of 0.037 compares against the actual rate of 0.016, producing the 58% reduction figure.' (quoted from PPC Land's write-up of the Ahrefs post)
Reuters DNR 2026: 'Google traffic from organic search to over 2,500 sites was down by a third (33%) globally between November 2024 and November 2025'.
Google I/O 2026 (MediaNama): 'Google said AI Mode has crossed 1 billion monthly users, while AI Overviews now reach 2.5 billion users every month.'

Pew (68,879 searches by 900 US adults, March 2025): 'Users who encountered an AI summary clicked on a traditional search result link in 8% of all visits' vs 15% without; links inside the summary were clicked in 'just 1% of all visits'.

sources.title: PPC Land on Ahrefs' Feb 2026 AI Overviews CTR update
Reuters Institute Digital News Report 2026
sources.supports: organic Google traffic to 2,500+ news sites down 33%

sources.title: Pew Research Center short read, July 2025
sources.supports: 8% vs 15% click rate with/without AI summary

items.note: Write pages whose value survives a summary: original data, tools, first-hand cases, opinions, templates, things the reader must click for. Judge informational posts by citations, brand mentions and conversions, not raw clicks; answer early but leave a reason to visit.

items.name: Generative engine optimisation (GEO / AEO): writing to be cited by AI search
items.one_line: Clients now ask for copy that AI Overviews, AI Mode, ChatGPT search and Perplexity will quote and cite, not just rank.

evidence.claim: Google Search Central guide 'Optimizing your website for generative AI features on Google Search': 'From Google Search's perspective, optimizing for generative AI search is optimizing for the search experience, and thus still SEO.'
Google I/O 2026: AI Mode 'has crossed 1 billion monthly users', AI Overviews 'reach 2.5 billion users every month'.
Reuters DNR 2026: '42% of AI chatbot users for news say they always or often click through from chatbot answers to original news sources'.

sources.title: Google Search Central: Optimizing your website for generative AI features on Google Search
sources.supports: Google's own position: GEO/AEO is SEO; non-commodity content

sources.title: Search Engine Journal: Google's new AI search guide calls AEO and GEO 'still SEO'
sources.supports: date and verbatim quotes of the guide

items.note: Lead each section with a direct, self-contained answer sentence; name entities, numbers and dates precisely; add a quotable original claim and first-hand evidence; keep pages indexable and snippet-eligible. Sell it as SEO writing done for answers, not as a separate trick.

items.name: llms.txt, chunking and AI-only rewrites: not needed for Google
items.one_line: Agencies push llms.txt files, chunked copy and AI-specific rewrites; Google's 2026 guide says none of that is required for its AI features.

evidence.claim: Google's AI-features guide: 'You don't need to create machine-readable files, AI text files, markup, or Markdown to appear in generative AI search.'

Same guide: 'There's no requirement to break content into small pieces for AI systems. Google's systems are able to understand the nuance.' and 'Site owners don't need to capture every long-tail keyword variation.'

sources.title: Google Search Central: Optimizing your website for generative AI features
sources.supports: no llms.txt / chunking / special markup needed

items.note: Write for people in clear sections with descriptive headings; do not bloat pages with keyword variants or split them into fragments for 'AI readability'. llms.txt may matter for other assistants, but do not bill it as a Google ranking factor.

items.name: Search enforcement against scaled AI content
items.one_line: Mass-produced AI pages are a named Google spam violation and 2026 updates kept targeting them; volume content is now a liability.

evidence.claim: Google spam policies: scaled content abuse includes 'Using generative AI tools or other similar tools to generate many pages without adding value for users'; the page also covers 'attempting to manipulate generative AI responses in Google Search'. 'Last updated 2026-08-28 UTC.'
Google's June 2026 spam update was announced on the Search Status Dashboard on 24 June 2026 and completed 26 June 2026 (third-party summary; low confidence on what it targeted).

sources.title: Google Search Central: Spam policies for Google web search
sources.supports: scaled content abuse definition incl. generative AI; AI-response manipulation

items.note: Sell fewer, better pages. Every AI-assisted draft needs added value: original examples, data, expert input, real editing. Push back on briefs for hundreds of near-identical programmatic pages (city pages, spun posts) with no unique substance per page.

items.name: First-hand, non-commodity content as the ranking and citation edge
items.one_line: Generic explainers are answered by AI; experience, original data and a point of view are what get ranked, cited and clicked.

evidence.claim: Google's May 2026 AI-search guide stresses 'non-commodity content' with unique, first-hand insight over generic guidance.
Pew: users ended their browsing session on '26% of pages with an AI summary, compared with 16% of pages with only traditional search results'.

sources.title: Google Search Central: Optimizing your website for generative AI features

items.note: Interview the client's experts, use their own numbers, screenshots, case results and opinions. Cut 'what is X' padding an AI summary already covers.

items.name: AI chatbots as a news and answer source
items.one_line: A growing minority, led by under-35s and Asian markets, get news and answers from chatbots instead of websites.

evidence.claim: Reuters DNR 2026: '10% of people use AI chatbots for news, up from 7% last year'.
GIJN summary of DNR 2026: growth driven largely by parts of Asia, Africa, Latin America and Southern/Eastern Europe; UK lowest at 4%; under-35s about three times the oldest group.

sources.title: Reuters Institute Digital News Report 2026

items.note: Write facts as clean, attributable sentences (who, what, number, date) with the brand or author name next to the claim, so a model lifting the sentence carries the attribution.

items.name: Ads inside AI assistants (ChatGPT ads)
items.one_line: ChatGPT started showing labelled ads beside answers in 2026, creating a new ad surface whose copy must match conversational intent.

evidence.claim: OpenAI: 'In the coming weeks, we're also planning to start testing ads in the U.S.'; 'Ads do not influence the answers ChatGPT gives you.'; 'Ads are always separate and clearly labeled.' Plus, Pro, Business and Enterprise stay ad-free.
TechCrunch: ChatGPT rolls out ads (US test for Free and Go tiers).

sources.title: OpenAI: Our approach to advertising and expanding access to ChatGPT

items.note: Treat assistant ads like search ads written for a conversation: answer the question the chat was about, one concrete benefit, plain CTA. Organic answer-quality content stays separate; ads cannot buy their way into the answer.

items.name: Product content written for AI shopping agents
items.one_line: Shoppers start delegating discovery and purchase to AI agents, so product copy must be machine-readable, specific and verifiable.

evidence.claim: ET BrandEquity on Accenture Consumer Pulse Survey 2026 (India): '70 per cent would like AI agents to shop in line with their personal goals'; '36 per cent indicated they would switch to another brand if an AI agent recommended a better option'; Accenture urges brands to ensure 'product information is machine-readable, pricing is transparent, claims are verifiable'.

sources.title: ET BrandEquity: Indian consumers embrace AI agent-led shopping, says Accenture
sources.supports: Indian consumer openness to agent shopping; AI-ready product info

items.note: Write product pages and feeds with complete attributes (size, material, ingredients, compatibility, price, warranty) in plain declarative sentences; back every claim with a spec or proof; drop vague superlatives an agent cannot verify.

items.name: AI search in Hindi and Indian languages
items.one_line: Google AI Mode and voice/camera Search Live now work in Hindi and seven more Indian languages, opening vernacular AI-search visibility.

evidence.claim: Google India: AI Mode rolling out in 'Bengali, Kannada, Malayalam, Marathi, Tamil, Telugu, and Urdu', plus 'Search Live in AI Mode to India in English and Hindi', India first outside the US.
IAMAI-Kantar Internet in India 2025: '44% of users engaging with AI-enabled features such as voice search, image-based search, chatbots, and AI filters'.

sources.title: Google India blog: new languages in AI Mode & Search Live
sources.supports: AI Mode in 7 Indian languages + Hindi Search Live

items.note: For Indian clients, publish answer-first pages in Hindi and the regional language, not only English; use conversational question headings that match spoken queries.

items.name: Rural, vernacular India drives internet growth
items.one_line: Most new Indian internet users are rural and consume in their own language, so Hindi/regional and Hinglish copy reaches the growth audience.

evidence.claim: IAMAI-Kantar report (Jan 2026): 'India now has 958 million Active Internet Users (AIU), marking an approximate 8% year-on-year growth'; 'rural India accounts for 57% of India's active internet users, i.e, approximately 548 million'; rural is 'growing at nearly four times the pace of urban India'.
Google expanded AI Mode to seven Indian languages beyond Hindi and English.

sources.title: YourStory on IAMAI-Kantar Internet in India Report 2025

items.note: Default to bilingual deliverables for mass-market Indian brands: a Hindi (Devanagari) or regional version, a Hinglish social version, and English for metros. Write native, not translated.

items.name: Short-form video is the mass format in India
items.one_line: Six in ten Indian internet users watch short video, so reel and Shorts scripts are the default brief for consumer brands.

evidence.claim: IAMAI-Kantar report: 'in 2025, 588 million (61%) internet users consumed short-video content, with rural users marginally outnumbering urban users'.
YouTube CEO letter: Shorts 'now averages 200 billion daily views'.

sources.title: IAMAI-Kantar Internet in India 2025 (via YourStory)
YouTube Official Blog: From the CEO, what's coming to YouTube in 2026

items.note: Write reel scripts first and articles second for B2C India: hook in the first line, one idea, on-screen text that works muted, Hinglish where the audience speaks it.

items.name: Vertical micro-dramas (scripted short series)
items.one_line: Minute-long episodic vertical dramas are India's fastest-growing entertainment format, creating demand for serial short-form scriptwriting.

evidence.claim: Storyboard18 on Redseer (report dated August 2026): micro-drama market could grow 10x to 'Rs 23,500-25,500 crore by FY32'; ad revenue 'from around Rs 24 crore in FY26 to Rs 210 crore in FY27E and eventually reach Rs 5,000-5,500 crore by FY32P'.

FICCI FRAMES 2026 (Eloelo CEO Saurabh Pandey): 'Microdrama is the quick-commerce moment for entertainment'; downloads in India 'roughly 60% to 65% of OTT downloads', users spend '60 to 70 minutes a day' (speaker claim).
YouTube: 'microdramas on YouTube surpassed 6.5 billion views, with watch time growing by over 50% year-over-year'; new Shorts Series lets creators 'structure their Shorts into seasons and episodes'.

sources.title: Storyboard18: Redseer micro-drama report
sources.supports: India market size and ad revenue forecasts

sources.title: YouTube Official Blog, Made on YouTube 2026

items.note: Learn episodic short scripting: cold-open hook in 3 seconds, one reversal per episode, cliffhanger last line, 60-90 s episodes, Hindi/Hinglish dialogue. Pitch brand-funded micro-series to D2C clients.

items.name: YouTube long-form watched on the TV screen
items.one_line: YouTube is increasingly watched on TVs, which rewards longer, produced, lean-back scripts over phone-only formats.

evidence.claim: YouTube: 'Over half of YouTube's top 100 creators have TV as their most watched interface'.
YouTube CEO letter: 'YouTube is the new TV because creators are the new prime time.'

sources.title: YouTube Official Blog, Made on YouTube 2026
sources.supports: TV as most-watched interface for top creators

sources.title: YouTube CEO letter 2026

items.note: For YouTube long-form, write like TV: cold open, chaptered acts, recaps for viewers joining late, visuals that read across a room, not 'tap the link below' as the only CTA.

items.name: Video podcasts and clip culture
items.one_line: Podcasts are now filmed shows cut into clips, so podcast work includes episode outlines, titles, clip hooks and show notes.

evidence.claim: Edison Research at SSRS, The Infinite Dial 2026: 'podcast and online audio consumption have reached all-time highs'; 84% of Americans 12+ use YouTube monthly (survey of 2,050 people, January 2026).
YouTube CEO letter lists podcasts among the formats viewers choose YouTube for, on 'every format on every screen'.

sources.title: Edison Research at SSRS: The Infinite Dial 2026

items.note: Offer podcast packages: guest research brief, cold-open clip pick, episode title and thumbnail text, 3-5 clip hooks for Shorts/Reels, chapter markers and show notes. YouTube-first titles beat audio-first titles. (YouTube's exact share of podcast listening was snippet-only in this sweep.)

items.name: News and explainer creators rival publishers
items.one_line: Individual creators now meet a real share of people's news needs, so personality-led explainers compete with brand media.

evidence.claim: Reuters DNR 2026: 'Around a quarter (27%) of respondents globally get some news from news-focused individual creators or influencers'; '13% of respondents say that most or all of their news needs are met by creators who focus on news'.
Reuters DNR 2026: '77% of people globally consume online news video each week'.

sources.title: Reuters Institute Digital News Report 2026
sources.supports: 27% / 13% creator news figures; 77% weekly news video

items.note: Script explainers in a person's voice (first person, opinion, to camera) rather than institutional copy; show sources on screen because trust is the creator's only asset.

items.name: Platforms reward originality and demote reposts and repetitive content
items.one_line: Instagram and YouTube cut reach for aggregators and mass-produced, repetitive content; original work with added value is what gets recommended.

evidence.claim: Instagram will 'no longer recommend photos and carousel posts from aggregator accounts within Explore and other surfaces'; 'If most of what an account posts within that 30-day period are re-posts, it will be considered an aggregator account.'
YouTube CEO letter: 'To reduce the spread of low quality AI content, we're actively building on our established systems ... reducing the spread of low quality, repetitive content.'

sources.title: Social Media Today: Instagram updates algorithm to benefit original creators
sources.supports: aggregator demotion extended to photos and carousels

sources.title: YouTube CEO letter 2026

items.note: Never ship templated, lightly varied posts at scale. Reaction or curation content must add commentary, data or a new angle; Instagram says edits must 'add real value beyond just simply restating or referencing the third-party content'.

items.name: Hashtags shrink; keyword-rich captions and on-screen text do the discovery work
items.one_line: Instagram capped hashtags at five, and social posts are found through search, so captions are written like search snippets.

evidence.claim: Instagram (Dec 2025): 'Using fewer (up to 5) more targeted hashtags, rather than many generic ones, can improve both your content's performance and people's experience on Instagram.'
From 10 July 2025 Meta let Google and Bing index public posts from professional Instagram accounts (third-party summary).

sources.title: Social Media Today: Instagram implements new limits on hashtag use

items.note: Put the searchable phrase in the first caption line and in on-screen text; use at most 3-5 specific hashtags; write captions that answer the question someone would type.

items.name: Threads becomes a mainstream text network
items.one_line: Threads passed 500 million monthly users and opened ads globally, making short text posts a growing brand channel again.

evidence.claim: Meta Q2 2026 earnings call: 'Threads crossed 500 million monthly actives, making it the fastest growing conversation app ever.' and 'we also expanded availability of ads on our newer surfaces, including completing our global ads expansion on Threads.'
Meta newsroom: new features to celebrate 500 million monthly users on Threads.

sources.title: Meta Q2 2026 earnings call transcript
Meta newsroom: Threads 500 million

items.note: Repurpose LinkedIn/X thinking into conversational Threads posts: one opinion, a question, no link in the main post; plan reply threads, not monologues.

items.name: WhatsApp as acquisition and AI-agent sales channel
items.one_line: Indian D2C brands now win first-time buyers on WhatsApp and Meta is putting AI business agents there, so conversational copy and flows are a paid deliverable.

evidence.claim: ET on a GoKwik report: 'About 83% of orders generated through WhatsApp during the October-December festive quarter came from first-time buyers'; brands using its WhatsApp tools saw median GMV growth '2.25 times higher'.
Meta Q2 2026: Business Agents are live globally on WhatsApp and Messenger, and 'there are already more than 1 million businesses using them to talk to their customers or complete sales every week'

sources.title: Economic Times: D2C brands turn to WhatsApp to win new customers
Meta Q2 2026 earnings call transcript

items.note: Write WhatsApp broadcasts and bot flows as short, permission-based, one-action messages; script agent personas, FAQs and escalation lines; follow template-category rules and opt-in.

items.name: LinkedIn becomes a creator and video platform
items.one_line: LinkedIn now pays creators via BrandLink video ads and ranks posts with a rebuilt LLM-assisted feed, pushing B2B writing toward video and personal expertise.

evidence.claim: BrandLink ad revenue-share now covers 'more than 100 creators and publishers', up from 30; LinkedIn is building a brand-deals marketplace, subscriptions and a creator fund for fiscal 2027 (per Business Insider-reviewed documents).

LinkedIn engineering post 'Engineering the next generation of LinkedIn's Feed' (Hristo Danchev) describes rebuilt ranking using LLM embeddings; 'The ranking model relies on professional signals and engagement patterns, and specifically excludes demographic attributes.'
CMI B2B 2026 research: 96% create thought leadership content and LinkedIn is the top channel for it at 76%.

sources.title: Social Day: LinkedIn BrandLink shares revenue with 100+ creators
PPC Land: LinkedIn rebuilds its feed with LLMs

items.note: Write LinkedIn posts that show topical expertise consistently (same 2-3 themes), invite substantive comments, and pair with short vertical video scripts. Treat '360Brew' claims as unconfirmed; LinkedIn's own posts describe a generative recommender.

items.name: Founder- and executive-led thought leadership
items.one_line: B2B buyers trust people over logos, so ghostwritten executive posts, POV essays and bylines are a core commissioned genre.

evidence.claim: CMI B2B Content and Marketing Trends for 2026: 96% of B2B organisations create thought leadership content; LinkedIn rated top channel (76%); 65% credit content relevance and quality for improved effectiveness.
LinkedIn BrandLink expansion pays individual creators and executives for video content (100+ participants).

sources.title: Content Marketing Institute: B2B Content and Marketing Trends, Insights for 2026
sources.supports: thought leadership adoption and LinkedIn channel effectiveness

items.note: Ghostwrite from recorded interviews with the executive; every post needs one specific experience, number or contrarian view only that person can claim. No generic 'lessons I learned' lists.

items.name: Paid newsletters and owned audiences
items.one_line: As platform reach and search clicks fall, brands and creators invest in email lists they own, and paid newsletters keep growing.

evidence.claim: beehiiv State of Paid Newsletters 2026: paid subscription revenue '$19 million in 2025, up 138% from 2024'; median free-to-paid conversion '0.62%'; share of revenue-earning users with paid subscriptions doubled from 15% (Q1 2024) to 30% (Q1 2026).

sources.title: beehiiv: The State of Paid Newsletters 2026
sources.supports: paid newsletter growth and conversion benchmarks

items.note: Pitch newsletter writing as an owned-channel hedge: one strong idea per issue, consistent format, a reason to forward. Expect under 1% free-to-paid; write the free tier to build trust, not to tease.

items.name: Creator-made content as paid ads (partnership ads, UGC)
items.one_line: Brands increasingly run creator posts as paid ads, so scripts are written for creators to perform and for ads to reuse.

evidence.claim: Meta at Cannes Lions 2026 will merge Creator Marketplace and Partnership Ads Hub into 'Meta Creator Marketing Hub' and make it easier for brands to find product-linked creator content and 'convert it into partnership ads'.
Forbes headline: 'Meta Partnership Ads Hit $10 Billion As Creators Outperform Brand Messages' (article body blocked; headline-only, low confidence).
Net Influencer: Meta turns creator livestreams into paid ads with new Instagram Live video ads.

sources.title: BuzzInContent: Meta builds single creator marketing hub

items.note: Write UGC/creator briefs, not finished scripts: hook options, must-say claims (with ASCI disclosure), proof moment, and a natural CTA the creator can say in their own words; plan 3-5 hook variants per ad.

items.name: Backlash against AI slop; human authenticity as a selling point
items.one_line: Audiences and platforms are turning against generic AI content, so visibly human, specific, accountable writing is a premium.

evidence.claim: Fortune: 'Over half (53%) of consumers distrust AI-generated search results and summaries, a 2025 survey by Gartner found'; YouTube's CEO named 'managing AI slop' a 2026 priority.

Ringer Sciences roundup: '40% of consumers say heavy AI use would decrease trust in a favorite brand — double the 20% in 2025 — Fractl, Q2 2026'; 42% would think less of a brand advertised beside low-quality AI content (DoubleVerify/YouGov). Secondary roundup; medium-low confidence.
YouTube CEO letter: 'The rise of AI has raised concerns about low-quality content, aka "AI slop."'

sources.title: YouTube CEO letter 2026
sources.supports: platform commitment to reduce AI slop

sources.title: Fortune: Businesses are declaring war on AI slop
sources.supports: consumer distrust stats and industry response

items.note: Strip AI tells (generic openers, tricolons, 'delve', empty hedges); add names, places, numbers, lived detail; let the brand's people be visible. Never claim 'human-written' unless true.

items.name: Mandatory AI-content labelling (India IT Rules 2026, EU AI Act Art. 50)
items.one_line: India and the EU now require labels on synthetic media and, in the EU, on unreviewed AI text about public-interest matters.

evidence.claim: Freshfields: India's IT Rules amendments (announced 10 Feb 2026, in force 20 Feb 2026) bring 'synthetically generated information' (audio, visual, audio-visual; AI text excluded) under prominent labelling, metadata and user-declaration duties for large platforms.

EU AI Act Article 50 transparency obligations apply from 2 August 2026; AI-generated text published to inform the public on matters of public interest must disclose its AI origin unless 'the AI-generated content has undergone a process of human review or editorial control and a natural or legal person holds editorial responsibility'.
YouTube: 'creators must disclose when they've created realistic altered or synthetic content.'

sources.title: artificialintelligenceact.eu: practical guide to Article 50
Freshfields: India targets deepfakes and AI-generated content

items.note: Keep a named human editor accountable for every AI-assisted piece (record who reviewed it). Label AI voice-overs, avatars and synthetic visuals in Indian and EU deliverables; write disclosure lines that are plain, not buried.

items.name: AI-assisted writing is the default workflow; editing AI output is the job
items.one_line: Nearly all marketing teams draft with AI, so clients pay for direction, editing, fact-checking and voice rather than first drafts.

evidence.claim: CMI B2B 2026 research: 89% of B2B marketers use AI tools for written content; only 9% prioritise human resources (salaries, training) in 2026 budget increases.

Upwork In-Demand Skills 2026: 'the top skills explicitly tied to applying AI within existing roles grew 109% year over year'; 'Professionals who can direct and refine AI outputs to enhance their work will stand out and find success.'

sources.title: CMI: B2B Content and Marketing Trends for 2026
sources.supports: AI use for writing; flat human budgets

sources.title: Upwork: In-Demand Skills 2026 press release

items.note: Position as editor-strategist: sell briefs, research, interviews, fact-checks and voice; disclose AI use to clients per contract; price by outcome or project, not per word.

items.name: AI video generation creates script and prompt work
items.one_line: AI video generation is the fastest-growing freelance skill, and every AI video still needs a script, shot list and prompts.

evidence.claim: Upwork In-Demand Skills 2026: Design & Creative fastest-growing 'AI Video Generation & Editing (+329%)' and 'AI Image Generation & Editing (+95%)' (US-demand freelancer earnings, 2025).
YouTube CEO letter: 'This year you'll be able to create a Short using your own likeness'.

sources.title: Upwork: In-Demand Skills 2026 press release

items.note: Bundle script + shot list + per-shot prompts + VO lines as one deliverable; write prompts as camera directions with continuity notes; disclose synthetic likeness where rules require.

items.name: Reddit and forum content in search and AI answers, with volatile referrals
items.one_line: Reddit threads surface in Google and feed AI answers, but Google referrals to Reddit swing, so community writing is a channel, not a guarantee.

evidence.claim: CNBC: Reddit DAUq 'jumped 18% year-over-year to 130.3 million'; the company said 'search referrals were choppy'; its two biggest data-licensing partners are OpenAI and Google.
gHacks (citing WSJ via TechSpot): Reddit and major publishers reevaluate Google access as AI Overviews cut search referral traffic.

sources.title: CNBC: Reddit Q2 2026 earnings
sources.supports: Reddit DAU and Google referral volatility

items.note: Write community answers as a genuine member: disclose affiliation, answer the actual question, no link-dropping. Brands should seed honest, specific answers that AI models and searchers can cite.

items.name: Inbox-provider rules punish spammy bulk and cold email
items.one_line: Gmail, Yahoo and Outlook enforce authentication, spam-rate and easy-unsubscribe rules for bulk senders, so mass AI cold email gets filtered.

evidence.claim: MarTech (updated June 2026): bulk-sender guidelines 'largely focus on three areas: authentication of outgoing emails, reported spam rates and the ability to easily unsubscribe'; Google defines bulk senders as 'those who send more than 5,000 messages to Gmail addresses in one day'; Microsoft applies similar rules to Outlook.com domains.

sources.title: MarTech: Bulk email restrictions from Google, Yahoo and Microsoft

items.note: Write fewer, more relevant emails: plain-text style, one ask, real personalisation from research (not merge-field flattery), a clear unsubscribe. Volume-based AI sequences hurt the domain.

items.name: Publishers and brands shift from search traffic to direct relationships
items.one_line: With search referrals falling, publishers and brands lean on video, creators, newsletters and apps for audience.

evidence.claim: Reuters DNR 2026: 'social media and video networks are, on average ..., more popular than both TV and owned news websites and apps as sources of news'.
Fortune quoting an industry source: 'Some businesses have seen organic search traffic decline by between 5% and 35% as AI answer engines provide instant responses'.

sources.title: Reuters Institute Digital News Report 2026

items.note: Every content plan needs an owned-audience path (newsletter, WhatsApp, community) and a video/creator path; measure success by subscribers and returning readers, not only sessions.
